I've farmed these 20 years in Quzhou. I finished middle school, then came straight back to the land. I have 16.1 mu and four mouths to feed at home. My wife and son work over in the county town at a factory, so when it gets busy I hire two local workers for a few days, but mostly I run it myself. I have a well, so I can pump water when the rain doesn't come.

I don't read farming books. I talk to Old Zhang at the input shop, and I watch what Lao Wang and the others do. If they try a new seed and their field looks better than mine, I switch the next year on one plot to test it. Last year my wheat made about 1,000 jin per mu, maize about 1,200 jin, cotton was a little low because of too much rain at flowering. This year I will do almost exactly the same as last year — change is risky, and I know what works.

My wheat is already in the ground on 10 mu. I planted it last October after rotary tilling. I use improved Jimai seed; I switched from the old local seed five years ago after Lao Wang's plot looked much better. For fertilizer, I put down one 50kg bag of 16-16-16 compound fertilizer per mu as base in autumn, and now in spring at jointing I topdress with 20kg of urea per mu. That adds up to about 17kg nitrogen, 6kg phosphorus, and 5kg potassium per mu for the whole season. I will irrigate three times — the return green water in March, the jointing water right now, and one more at heading in May. I spray pesticide twice: once for aphids when I see them, and once for powdery mildew if the weather turns damp. I expect about 510kg per mu if the late spring wind doesn't damage it.

After I harvest wheat in early June, I plant summer maize on the same 10 mu. There is almost no time to waste, so I rotary till fast and plant hybrid Zhengdan 958. Everyone around here plants Zhengdan 958 — the stalk is strong and it doesn't fall over in the summer storms. At planting I put 40kg of compound fertilizer per mu, then at big flare mouth stage I topdress with 15kg of urea per mu. That is 16kg nitrogen, 5kg phosphorus, and 5kg potassium per mu total. Maize doesn't need as much water as people think if you hit the right times, so I irrigate twice: once when the tassel comes out, and once at grain filling. Two pesticide sprays are enough. I expect 600kg per mu.

My remaining 6.1 mu is cotton. I plough deep in spring because cotton roots need to go deep, and they can't push through hard soil. I plant improved Bt cotton seed. For fertilizer, I put one 50kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu as base, then topdress twice with urea during flowering and boll stage — about 10kg each time. That comes to about 15kg nitrogen, 5kg phosphorus, and 7kg potassium per mu for the year. Cotton needs water when the flowers open, so I irrigate three times. Even with Bt cotton, I spray four times because the aphids and spider mites still come — I don't trust the seed to do everything. I expect 280kg per mu of seed cotton.

I think about every yuan. Fertilizer prices went up again this year. But I have over 15 mu, so I can absorb the cost. Better to put a little too much than too little. If I lose yield, the whole year is ruined. If I waste half a bag of urea, that's only 100 yuan lost. I watch my neighbors and match them. If Lao Wang puts more fertilizer on his wheat this spring, I put more too.
